To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) there is evidence of the existence of a growth regime in which exports are a major determinant of growth; (ii) this regime is more likely to appear in the North than in the South, where the growth process is supply constrained; (iii) this is due to the role played by efficiency‐enhancing variables such as technological innovation, the diffusion of banks and social capital.

(i) demand‐constrained manufacturing growth regimes are more likely to be observed in regions with high levels of productive efficiency, and (ii) the dispersion of growth regimes in Italy is mainly explained by the dispersion of efficiency.

(i) demand‐constrained manufacturing output is positively correlated with exports in Italian regions; (ii) supply‐side factors are relevant to explain the dispersion in the regional distribution of demand‐constrained output; (iii) the role of efficiency‐enhancing supply‐side factors is greater than that of labour market rigidities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a neglected issue: the role of supply‐side efficiency in explaining growth regimes.
the role of demand and supply constraints in explaining regional growth.
the determinants of growth regimes in Italy and with the role played by the export sector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the supply constraints on growth in the Italian economy are not related to labour market rigidities, but are more likely to be related to the efficiency with which resources are employed.
, in Italy, the demand‐constrained regime is not widespread and that supply‐side efficiency factors play a key role in determining the dispersion of regional growth regimes.

, in the Italian case, the growth of the manufacturing sector has a strong demand‐driven component, and that this component is not equally distributed among Italian regions, with the South being the region most affected by this phenomenon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regional differences in growth regimes are explained by regional differences in efficiency factors.
regional differences in supply constraints are the main determinant of regional differences in growth regimes.
the Italian economy is not characterized by a uniform growth regime, but rather by a variety of growth regimes, which differ across regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the Italian case, growth performance may be improved through the enhancement of supply‐side efficiency.
, in order to explain the regional dispersion of economic growth, we need to take into account the regional dispersion of both demand‐ and supply-side factors.
the role of supply constraints in determining regional differences in growth regimes is not negligible.
